findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext in the instance user_data script. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone who gains any code execution or SSRF on the host, and it is stored unencrypted in the EC2 API and Terraform state.
No root_block_device/ebs_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance's EBS volumes may be created unencrypted, leaving data at rest unprotected.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled; combined with a publicly reachable web server this makes credential theft via SSRF straightforward, and the user_data secrets are exposed through the metadata endpoint.

The instance is launched in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a security group open to 0.0.0.0/0, giving it a routable public IP and direct exposure to the internet including SSH.
Ingress on TCP port 22 is allowed from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.

Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 (cleartext HTTP with no TLS alternative configured) and egress is unrestricted to all ports/protocols/destinations, which permits data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true (the attribute is explicitly commented out), so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted.

The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume and specifies no encryption, so a copy of the volume's data persists unencrypted and can be shared or restored by anyone with snapshot permissions.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so network flow records containing internal IP topology are stored unencrypted.

No public access block, bucket ACL restriction, versioning, or TLS-only bucket policy is configured for the flow log bucket, leaving it reliant on defaults and vulnerable to accidental public exposure or tampering with audit data.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP address, removing the network boundary and exposing workloads directly to the internet via the attached internet gateway.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP address, and the subnet is routed to the internet gateway, so no private network segment exists in this VPC.
